short: SALL1 to SALL4 are the human Spalt-like proteins: large C2H2 zinc-finger factors built from several clusters of paired fingers, with a short N-terminal motif that recruits the NuRD corepressor complex. Their DNA binding is unusual in being defined by base composition rather than by a sequence. A single C-terminal pair of fingers in SALL4 reads AT-rich DNA, and a crystal structure shows why it is promiscuous: the contacts use small side chains in the major groove, so many different AT-rich combinations are accepted. There is consequently no reliable consensus string for this family. SALL1 mutations cause Townes-Brocks syndrome and SALL4 mutations Okihiro syndrome; SALL4 is also the cereblon substrate whose degradation explains thalidomide limb teratogenicity.
long:
## The factors

The four human SALL genes, SALL1 to SALL4, are homologues of Drosophila spalt. Each protein is large
and built from several clusters of C2H2 zinc fingers, usually a set of paired fingers (three or four
double-finger clusters) plus one unpaired finger, separated by long low-complexity linkers. A short
motif at the extreme N terminus recruits the nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase (NuRD) complex,
and NuRD recruitment accounts for much of the repressive activity attributed to these proteins; the
same interaction is required for SALL4's contribution to reprogramming. SALL4 is highly expressed in
embryonic stem cells and in germ-cell and hepatocellular tumors but silenced in most adult tissues,
which is why it is used as an immunohistochemical marker. SALL1 is prominent in kidney and limb,
SALL3 in the nervous system. Mouse work shows Sall1, Sall2 and Sall4 are each required for neural
tube closure.

## The motif

Only one of the SALL clusters binds DNA in SALL4: a pair of fingers near the C terminus (ZFC4).
Inactivating that one cluster drastically reduces SALL4's genome occupancy and reproduces the
phenotype of a complete Sall4 knockout, including precocious differentiation of embryonic stem cells
and embryonic lethality, whereas deleting two of the other clusters is phenotypically neutral. What
that cluster reads is AT-richness rather than a defined word: SALL4 was recovered in a screen for
proteins that bind AT-rich motifs, and genes are de-repressed on SALL4 loss in proportion to their AT
content. Protein-binding-microarray and CUT&RUN experiments define an AT-rich consensus, and the
crystal structure of the C-terminal fingers on AT-rich DNA explains the flexibility: recognition uses
small hydrophobic and polar side chains in the major groove, so many different combinations of A and
T are accepted. We therefore give no consensus string for this family; any single IUPAC word
overstates what the protein specifies.

The database situation reflects this awkwardly. Of the three matrices assigned here, only the SALL3
model (consensus TTATGAATTATGATAT, HOCOMOCO grade A with HT-SELEX, integrative and ChIP support) is
the AT-rich motif the literature describes, and it has no close neighbor among the other family
members. The SALL1 and SALL4 models are ChIP-only (grades C and B) and are GC-rich, with the
consensus GGGTGGGG, which is also the family's data consensus and its medoid. GGGTGGGG is a GC-box-
and KLF/SP-like sequence, and the most economical explanation is that these ChIP-derived models
capture a co-occupancy or promoter signal rather than SALL binding preference. Cohesion in this
family is 0.51, essentially because the literature motif and the database medoid disagree.

## Where it acts

SALL4 occupancy is broad and follows base composition: it accumulates over long AT-rich domains and
at AT-rich genes, a distribution unlike the punctate enhancer occupancy of most transcription
factors, and it acts largely to hold such genes down. That makes the relevant genomic feature a
region rather than a site. Reported partners include NuRD and, in pluripotent cells, the core
pluripotency factors. SALL1 in kidney and limb, and SALL4 in limb and heart development, act at
developmental enhancers, but no well-validated composite element carrying a named SALL site is
established in the way that exists for, say, GATA or ETS composites.

## Biology and disease

Heterozygous truncating SALL1 mutations cause Townes-Brocks syndrome (imperforate anus, thumb
malformations, dysplastic ears and hearing loss, with variable renal and cardiac involvement).
Heterozygous SALL4 mutations cause Okihiro (Duane-radial ray) syndrome, which overlaps the
radial-ray phenotype of Holt-Oram syndrome and includes Duane anomaly. The SALL4 phenotype is
mechanistically informative in two directions. First, the Okihiro missense mutations that fall inside
the C-terminal fingers reduce overall DNA binding without abolishing the AT preference and shift the
protein's association with AT-rich genomic sites, which supports their pathogenicity. Second, SALL4
is a thalidomide-dependent cereblon neosubstrate: thalidomide and its analogs recruit SALL4 to
cereblon for degradation, and this provides a molecular explanation for thalidomide limb
teratogenicity, since chemical SALL4 loss phenocopies genetic SALL4 loss. A crystal structure of the
SALL4-pomalidomide-cereblon-DDB1 complex shows how the degron is presented.

## Reading a hit

There is little to read. This family specifies base composition rather than a word, so a PWM hit is
close to meaningless on its own: an AT-rich match is expected anywhere in AT-rich DNA, and the same
matrices score homeodomain, forkhead and poly-A sequence. The four paralogues are not separable, and
in these databases only SALL1, SALL3 and SALL4 have models at all. The specific trap is the opposite
of the usual one: if your hit came from the GC-rich GGGTGGGG matrices labelled SALL1 or SALL4, you
have almost certainly matched a GC-box-like sequence, and a KLF, SP or other GC-box factor is the
more likely direct binder; those two models are ChIP-only and disagree with every in vitro
measurement of SALL4 specificity. A credible SALL4 claim rests on AT-rich domain-level enrichment,
on the effect of degrading or mutating the ZFC4 cluster, or on the clinical genetics, not on a motif
match.
caveats: SALL proteins read base composition, not a word: a C-terminal finger pair in SALL4 binds AT-rich DNA promiscuously, and the crystal structure shows the contacts accept many A/T combinations. We give no consensus for that reason, and an AT-rich hit is expected throughout AT-rich DNA and overlaps homeodomain, forkhead and poly-A signals. The paralogues are indistinguishable, and SALL2 has no model here. Worse, the family's medoid and data consensus come from ChIP-only SALL1 and SALL4 matrices that are GC-rich (GGGTGGGG, a GC-box/KLF-like sequence) and contradict every in vitro measurement; cohesion is 0.51. Matches to those two models are most likely GC-box factors, not SALL.
